- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.00) — especially after recent spikes — and adjust downward by 2–5% for the next 3–5 days.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment periods (sentiment < 0.00) — particularly when sentiment turns negative — and adjust upward by 2–5% for the next 3–5 days.
- Avoid over-optimistic forecasts after recent price spikes; reduce forecasted momentum by 10–20% in the immediate 3–5 day horizon.
- Mean-reversion bias is common in 30-day forecasts — if forecast is > 20% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 10–15%.
- If sentiment is 0.00 and price is trending upward, slightly reduce forecast slope to avoid over-leveraging bullish momentum.
- If sentiment is 0.00 and price is trending downward, slightly increase forecast slope to avoid under-reacting to bearish signals.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in the first 5 days of the 30-day horizon — apply a 5–10% downward correction for early days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is positive and price is rising, forecast should not exceed 1.5x the 18-day average — otherwise, cap at 1.5x to avoid over-optimism.
